02 / 06selected workok

The work

show, don't tell← the fun part

Personal R&D from my @megballcreates lab. These are the workflows I build, break and teach on my own time, long before they're ready for a team.

It used to begin with a sketch. Now it begins with a conversation.

I treat every new model like a new teammate. I figure out what it's good at, wire it into a real creative workflow, and write down what I learned so other people can skip the 2am part. Here are three builds I'm proud of.

  • Mood → marketA full product line from one moodboard
    01
  • Editorial → tech packPulling the garment out of the picture
    02
  • Idea → product pageFrom a conversation to a PDP
    03
01
Mood → market · Orchid Nebula

One moodboard. One prompt chain. A whole product line.

What if AI inspiration could turn into something a merchant could actually plan with? I started with nine campaign images and had Claude read them like a creative director and a planner at the same time: color, competitors, fabric, pricing and SKU architecture. Then I batch-exported every style as structured prompts into a Weavy pipeline.

40+
styles designed across suiting, prints, evening and accessories
200+
AI-ready prompts: hero, detail, editorial and flat sketch per style
4
capsules in one color architecture
13
competitors mapped across luxury, accessible and value tiers
Swipe the process

A few of the 42 styles

Every render uses the same brand prefix and one seed per style, so the collection still looks like one brand at 168 images, not just at one.

Prompts as data

// excerpt from the batch export
{
  "collection": "Orchid Nebula",
  "season": "Fall 2027",
  "total_styles": 42,
  "total_images": 168,
  "seed_strategy": "Same seed per style across prompt types",
  "styles": [{
    "style_id": "NC-001",
    "product_name": "Nebula Peak Lapel Blazer",
    "capsule": "Nebula Core",
    "pantone": "19-4005 TCX Moonless Night",
    "fabric": "97% Merino Wool / 3% Elastane",
    "retail_price": "$595",
    "prompts": {
      "hero_pdp":       { "use_case": "PDP Hero Image" },
      "detail_texture": { "use_case": "PDP Detail Image" },
      "editorial":      { "use_case": "Lookbook / Campaign" },
      "flat_sketch":    { "use_case": "Tech Pack Flat" }
    }
  }]
}

Each style ships as a structured record with fabric, trims, Pantone, price and four prompt types, so it can go into any generator and come out on-brand.

02
Editorial → tech pack · Weavy + Nano Banana

Pull the garment out of the picture.

Designers fall for an editorial image, and then someone has to turn that feeling into a spec. This workflow does the first pass. It lifts the garment off the model as a clean product flat, draws a line sketch for the tech pack, and pulls the print so you can recolor it. Drag the slider to see it work.

EditorialExtracted
  1. Drop in an editorialAny campaign or runway-style image.
  2. Extract the garmentA clean, front-facing flat on a neutral ground.
  3. Sketch itA black-and-white line drawing, ready for the tech pack.
  4. Lift the printIsolate the pattern, then swap new ones back in.

Flat, flat, then line sketch, all from one editorial shot.

One look, four prints. The swatches come straight out of the extraction step.

The working canvas, sped up.

03
Idea → product page · To the Moon

From a conversation to the product page.

A celestial capsule built without a sketchbook. An LLM reads the moodboard and writes the design briefs. Those briefs drive the product renders, macro details, e-commerce shots and the campaign, all inside one connected canvas.

The ideation canvas, sped up.

  1. Moodboard in21 images run through an image iterator.
  2. An LLM writes the briefsIt reads each image like an apparel, handbag and shoe designer would.
  3. Briefs become a listNamed concepts like Shadow Ankle Boots and Cloud Strap Boots.
  4. Renders outEach brief goes to an image model for product shots.

04 / 06how i workok

How I work

AI should make creative work better and more fun, not more complicated.

I start from the people doing the work. The technology comes second, and it has to earn its place.

  • Strategy to productionI lead creative AI strategy and the messy middle nobody talks about, so pilots actually ship — across design, product, marketing, sales and studio.
  • Workflows across the whole lifecycleConcept, product visualization, artwork and print, content, retailer presentations and asset reuse, all connected.
  • Responsible AI that holds upGovernance, risk classification, licensor restrictions and asset traceability. In licensed fashion, this is what separates a demo from production.
  • The ecosystemVendor evaluation, enterprise onboarding and partnerships across generative AI, creative tech, 3D, PLM and content platforms.

My rollout playbook: TEAR

from my keynote
T
Test

Put a tool in real hands, on a real brief, fast.

E
Evaluate

Judge it by the work: quality, speed and cost per approved asset.

A
Adopt

Train people, write the playbook and find the champions.

R
Rollout

Scale what earned it, with governance built in from day one.
